## The four plus neutral

1. mā, high and flat, like holding a note
2. má, rising, like "huh?"
3. mǎ, low dip, in real speech mostly just low and creaky
4. mà, sharp fall, like telling a dog "no!"
5. ma, neutral, light and short

Teacher Wang Li (王老师) on Preply, $19 a lesson, Tuesdays 19:00 Lisbon time, says my 1st tone sags at the end like
a tired balloon.

## Tone pairs drill

20 combinations (4 × 4 + neutral endings). Every morning I read the pair grid out loud: 飞机 fēijī (1-1), 中国
zhōngguó (1-2), 老师 lǎoshī (3-1), 再见 zàijiàn (4-4). Recording myself on the Pleco flashcards, 10 minutes. Works
best combined with [[Shadowing technique]].

## Sandhi rules

- 3 + 3 → 2 + 3: 你好 is said ní hǎo
- 不 bù becomes bú before a 4th tone: 不是 bú shì
- 一 yī becomes yí before a 4th tone, yì before 1st, 2nd, 3rd: 一个 yí ge, 一天 yì tiān

## My problem pairs

2-3 and 3-2 collapse into the same mush. Classic disaster: 买 mǎi (buy) vs 卖 mài (sell) at a market stall in
Beijing, the seller thought I wanted to sell her my water bottle. Full story in [[北京胡同]]. Also 四 sì vs 十 shí,
which is less a tone problem than a retroflex problem.

## Food words as practice

Ordering in my Lisbon Sichuan place is my weekly test: 麻婆豆腐 mápó dòufu is 2-2-4-0, and I finally got it right in
October 2024. Recipe I cook at home: [[麻婆豆腐]].
